item.title: Oriel 3.1.1
item.description:
Swipe two fingers up on a text, a Live Activity or a song's title to send it away

Swipe two fingers up on the island to hide it in the notch (the music glow can stay); swipe down or click the notch to bring it back

A hidden island comes back on its own after you've been away for an hour

Scroll over the calendar with two fingers or your mouse wheel to move between weeks and months

Share files from the tray to Messages, Mail, Notes and more, not just AirDrop

Clearer messages when Claude usage needs you to sign in to Claude Code again

Contact photos only show for the right person (a notification from an app like X no longer borrows a friend's photo)

A smoother animation when the island tucks into the notch and comes back

Fixed Live Activities showing as a black card while the island was hidden

item.title: Oriel 3.1
item.description:
The island tucks into the notch while you watch videos in full screen, and stays for your music

When several things happen at once, the most important comes first (calls, then texts), and the rest wait their turn

Fewer interruptions: keep Claude, timers, downloads and more beside the notch, always or only during a Focus

A Usage widget shows your Claude and Codex limits right in the island

Updates now install overnight on their own, and a "What's new" window shows what changed

Lock screen: with the cover showing, the song moves to the middle, like the iPhone

Focus changes show your Focus's own icon and colour (custom ones too), and can be turned off

While you reply to a text, your other unread texts stay in view

The charging battery is back, filled to your level like iOS 27's

Calls pick up faster when you click Answer

AirPods show once, in Oriel's island card

Live Activities on the lock screen shrink to fit while lyrics show

A switch to turn off the glow when the island is tucked away

Starting a video no longer flashes a grey cover over your music

Fixed a play button that could keep a grey circle around it

item.title: Oriel 3.0.4
item.description:
Clicking an email opens it in its own app (Mail, Outlook, Spark, Gmail in your browser and more), and Mail shows it in its main window

A reply you're writing stays open until you click somewhere else

AirPods and other devices no longer show twice; with the island open, their card appears just below it, like macOS's own

Controllers that can't report their battery no longer show 100%

Liquid Glass can now be clear as water: drag Shade all the way to Clear

Remixes and edits show the original song's lyrics, and the island steps out of the way of menus faster

item.title: Oriel 3.0.3
item.description: Texts, calls, meetings, widgets and more are now on for everyone (anything you switched off stays off); macOS asks about what they need, and a no turns just that off

item.title: Oriel 3.0.2
item.description:
Lyrics stay in time with Spotify and Apple Music

Instrumental breaks show Apple Music's three dots, and lines no longer crawl through them

Lyrics show up reliably, even when the lyrics service is busy

The big player's play button slides smoothly with the other buttons

New installs start with everything on; say no to a permission and just that feature turns off

item.title: Oriel 3.0.1
item.description:
Widgets are safer: only the Oriel gallery can add one in a click, and widgets from anywhere else are clearly marked as not reviewed

Widgets can no longer read from your Mac or your local network

When two contacts share a number, texts show the number instead of guessing who sent them

item.title: Oriel 3.0
item.description:
The island grew up: a big player in the notch with synced lyrics, Up Next, volume and output, for Apple Music and Spotify

Moving album covers (Apple Music's animated art) in the island, the big player, full screen and your lock screen

Your music on the Mac's lock screen, with its controls and lyrics

Live Activities: Claude Code and Codex step by step (a red ! when they need you), Pomodoro timer, downloads, screen recording, meetings with mute and leave, charging and AirPods

Texts and emails out of the notch, with the photos people send and the right profile pictures; reply right from the island; read on your iPhone and they clear here

Calls ring in the island with Answer and Decline (turn on "Show who's calling" to see the caller's name)

Shazam in the island, one click to the song in Apple Music, Spotify or YouTube

Calendar: add events by typing ("lunch with Rita tomorrow 1pm"), reminders you can tick off, your week, meeting alerts with Join

File tray: drop files on the notch, drag them out or AirDrop them; clipboard history, quick notes and a mirror

Widgets: weather, batteries, system, reminders, world clock, and widgets anyone can make (builder and gallery on the website)

Your AI limits for Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and Copilot at a glance

Spotify: save to Liked Songs, see which playlists a song is in, see where it's playing and move it to another device

Black, Liquid Glass or glass tinted by the song; swipe on the island to skip; it tucks away when menus need the room

Works with macOS 27, follows Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency, and stays light: about 47 MB of memory, under 1% CPU at rest

item.title: Oriel 2.3
item.description:
Oriel 2.3

  • Spotify login in the Keychain. Your Spotify login is now stored encrypted in the macOS Keychain, readable only by Oriel and never synced. It moves over automatically.
  • Hardened runtime. macOS now blocks other programs from injecting code into Oriel.
  • Less on disk. A leftover debug log is gone, along with old copies of it.
  • Safer Apple Music commands. Extra checks on what Oriel sends to Music.

item.title: Oriel 2.2
item.description:
Oriel 2.2

  • AirPlay like the Music app. With Apple Music, or Spotify without a login, the AirPlay button opens the same AirPlay menu as macOS, and the island stays open while you pick.
  • Send Feedback. Ideas, bugs or questions? Settings → General → Send Feedback opens an email to orielformac@gmail.com.
  • New website. Oriel now has a home at orielformac.pages.dev.
  • Tidier under the hood. Your settings and Spotify login move to a new folder automatically; nothing to do.

item.title: Oriel 2.1
item.description:
Oriel 2.1

  • Spotify login is now optional. Spotify works straight away, no setup. Log in from Settings only if you want saving, playlists and control of your other devices. Features that need the login stay hidden until you do.
  • Switching devices keeps your song. Moving Spotify from your phone to your Mac carries on with the same song, at the same second, without restarting DJ or losing your queue.
  • Smarter music bars. They hold still when music is playing on your phone or TV, like on iPhone, and start and stop the instant you press play or pause.
  • Calendar refresh. Today is red, weekends are a subtle bold white, and clicking the month opens Calendar.
  • New blue icon.
  • Fixes. The island stays put when you swipe between desktops, leaves macOS's volume and brightness pop-ups alone, and AirPods banners show the right picture for each device.

item.title: Oriel 2.0
item.description:
Meet Oriel 🎉

An oriel is a small window that juts out from the top of a wall, just like the island coming out of your notch.

New in 2.0

  • AirPods banners from the notch. "Connected" with battery, and "Moved to iPhone" with Undo, now come out of the island in Apple's design instead of the corner.
  • Spotify on any device. Playing on your phone or a speaker? It shows in the island, the controls work, and one click brings it back to your Mac.
  • New calendar. Today plus the week ahead (or the whole month in Settings), Apple-style dots, Google and other calendars, and "No events today" when your day is free.
  • Morning agenda. The first time you unlock your Mac each day, the island shows today's events.
  • Click through. Click the song or album to open it, and each artist on its own.
  • Glow. When an app's menus need the space, the island tucks into the notch and glows in the album's colour.
  • Steadier. The island stays put when you swipe between spaces and full-screen apps, uses much less battery, and leaves macOS's volume and brightness pop-ups alone.
  • Updates in the app. From now on, new versions show up right in Oriel.
  • Tidier Settings. Organised into General, Music, Calendar and Permissions, plus Uninstall.

Install

  1. Download Oriel.dmg below and drag Oriel to Applications.
  2. Open it. The first time, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.

Needs macOS 14 or newer.
